title: Mechanistic insight into signal bias by the agonist-dependent conformational dynamics of GPR84
abstract:
Nature Communications, Published online: 16 July 2026; doi:10.1038/s41467-026-75728-9

Authors here solve cryo-EM structures of the immune receptor GPR84, which reveal how a ‘biased’ drug favors one signaling pathway over another. A single steric clash inside the receptor acts as the switch, guiding the design of safer, more selective drugs.

title: Amine/ammonium buffering enables efficient anti-Markovnikov hydroamination of olefins with alkylamines
abstract:
Nature Communications, Published online: 16 July 2026; doi:10.1038/s41467-026-75644-y

Authors present an anti-Markovnikov hydroamination of olefins with alkylamines using an amine/ammonium buffering system under photocatalytic conditions. Key to this strategy is mitigating deprotonation of the involved aminium radical cation intermediate, formed through single electron oxidation of the associated alkylamine substrate, ensuring its effective addition to alkenes.

title: Interactively addressable organic metadevices
abstract:
Nature Communications, Published online: 16 July 2026; doi:10.1038/s41467-026-75757-4

An interactively addressable organic metadevice enables independent electrical control of metasurface pixels to generate reconfigurable holographic projections, providing a platform for programmable and user-interactive photonic systems.

title: Inhibited radiative decay enhances single-photon emitters
abstract:
Nature Communications, Published online: 16 July 2026; doi:10.1038/s41467-026-75489-5

Spin–photon interfaces for quantum networks often rely on resonator enhanced emission, limiting scalability and requiring precise tuning. Here, the authors demonstrate an alternative approach that avoids these limitations by suppressing unwanted radiative decay channels of erbium dopants using silicon photonic crystal waveguides.

title: Non-Destructive Blade Sharpness Characterization Using a High-Shear Responsive Fluid and Analytical Drag Modeling
abstract:
Nature Communications, Published online: 15 July 2026; doi:10.1038/s41467-026-75558-9

The study presents a non-destructive method for blade sharpness evaluation using a shear-responsive fluid and analytical drag modeling, enabling micron-scale sensitivity and whole-edge assessment with negligible material loss.

title: Direct Amidation of Alkynes with Nitroarenes via Heterogeneous Semiconductor TiO₂ Nanotubes
abstract:
Nature Communications, Published online: 15 July 2026; doi:10.1038/s41467-026-75432-8

Amide synthesis typically depends on wasteful condensation chemistry and harsh amidation conditions. Here, the authors report a visible-light-driven photocatalytic strategy using recyclable TiO₂ nanotubes to couple alkynes and nitroarenes enabling sustainable amide synthesis.

title: CenSegNet: a generalist high-throughput deep learning framework for centrosome phenotyping at spatial and single-cell resolution in heterogeneous tissues
abstract:
Nature Communications, Published online: 15 July 2026; doi:10.1038/s41467-026-75393-y

Cheng, Fan, and colleagues develop CenSegNet, a generalist AI framework for large-scale mapping of centrosome phenotypes, uncovering distinct patterns associated with breast tumour heterogeneity, disease progression and clinical outcomes.

title: Low-temperature liquid-assisted vibrational stress-relief strategy enables stable and efficient perovskite solar cells
abstract:
Nature Communications, Published online: 15 July 2026; doi:10.1038/s41467-026-75629-x

Perovskite solar cells face defects and interfacial strain that limit efficiency and stability, while standard chemical fixes can add stress. Yang et al. use low-temperature liquid-assisted vibration to remove defects and stress, improving efficiency, durability, and scalability.
